scope: Item 20 exact batch-local identities for repeated short text and composite grouping keys
baseline_policy: Reuse the complete locally accepted numeric observation and independently validated references. Continue all remaining item 20 in existing PR 1619; hosted acceptance remains separate. Do not rerun the baseline.
frozen_mechanisms: Extend the existing batch-local proved-identity cache to one or two integer, boolean, null or raw short-text/binary keys. A fixed exact representation can only return a group after ordinary native RowIndex has proved that complete key in this same batch. Hash collisions compare the complete cache identity and can only cause misses. New batches clear the cache.

Keep the existing single integer/dictionary directory first. For other eligible keys, admit a bounded 512-slot cache only for batches of at least 512 rows with at least 32 exact repeat hits in the first 256 rows, and only when its entire allocation is at most one sixteenth of available operator memory. Sampling is admission evidence only and cannot publish group identities.

Integer identities retain exact original signed/unsigned values and nulls; short text/binary identities normalize unused inline padding and distinguish NULL from empty and embedded NUL values. Long values, unsupported types, dictionary composite keys, sparse reuse, tiny batches and pressure retain ordinary exact native lookup. No key is ignored and output ownership/cancellation/failure order remains intact.
